articles.summary: ⚽ All the latest football news heading into the weekend ⚽ Ten things to look out for | Football Daily | Email Simon. Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle says he is uninterested in dwelling on what might have been when highly-rated Aston Villa midfielder Johan Manzambi visits St James’ Park this…
body: Manzambi looked set for a switch to Tyneside over the summer but the deal was hijacked as Villa swooped in to sign the Switzerland international, who has flourished during his short time in the midlands.

The 21-year-old opened the scoring in Villa’s 6-0 Champions League rout of Fenerbahce in midweek and he could rub salt into his former suitors’ wounds when Newcastle welcome Unai Emery’s side on Saturday.

But while Jaissle, who succeeded Eddie Howe after Manzambi snubbed a move to the north-east, is a fan of the youngster, the German side-stepped the question of whether he would have liked him in his ranks.

“He is a really good player,” said Jaissle, who will be looking for a response after Monday’s 4-1 loss at Coventry. “But I’m not here to talk now about players, about rumours, about potential signings. The pure focus is on our players. We have many things to do, many things to improve, and that’s the approach to not get distracted by anything else.”

articles.title: Australia v Samoa: women’s Rugby League World Cup – live
articles.summary: Updates as the Jillaroos and Fetu Samoa meet in the opener Sydney. Kick-off time is 8.05pm AEDT/10.05pm NZDT/10.05am BST. Any thoughts? Get in touch with an email. Hello and welcome to the opening game for the women’s competition at the Rugby League World Cup.
body: While the Jillaroos are heavy favourite for this game, don’t underestimate Fetu Samoa. With eight members of the Gold Coast Titans NRLW team in their squad, they will have some strong connections and plenty of passion.

The Jillaroos are looking to back up their 2022 World Cup win by taking out the trophy on home soil, and while they are confident they have the team to do it, they are wary of the rapid improvement of other nations.
“We are here with the mindset that we are going up against tough teams, everyone has been in an NRLW system,” said coach Jess Skinner, speaking to nrl.com.

“It’s going to be a lot tougher for us this year, but we are up for the challenge. I am really excited to see what Samoa does in this World Cup - what they did to the Kiwis in the last Pac Champs was very exciting.

articles.title: Kartal upsets Svitolina to reach Wuhan semi-finals
articles.summary: Sonay Kartal's winning streak following a long injury lay-off continues as she seals a hard-fought victory over fifth seed Elina Svitolina in the quarter-finals of the Wuhan Open.
body: The 24-year-old Briton, who missed more than six months with a stress fracture in her back, beat Ukrainian Svitolina 6-2 2-6 6-4 to mark her sixth win in eight matches since returning from injury.
It was another eye-catching performance by Kartal, who defeated Italian 15th seed Jasmine Paolini and Swiss ninth seed Belinda Bencic in the previous rounds.
She will face 2017 French Open champion Jeļena Ostapenko, who came through a tense opening set to beat 11th seed Diana Shnaider 7-6 (8-6) 6-1, in her first WTA 1000 semi-final on Saturday.
Speaking on court after her victory, Kartal said she knew "what a great fighter" world number six Svitolina is, so she "was never safe" in the match.

articles.title: Do Premier League teams really need to run more to win matches?
articles.summary: Pundits regularly criticise teams for not running enough but is there a link between distance covered and results? By Opta Analyst. It was like clockwork. Manchester United dropped points against Tottenham and critics were quick to question their effort and application, using the team’s physical…
body: Speaking on Sky Sports, Jamie Redknapp said: “There’s a pattern I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when – and the stats don’t lie – the other team runs more than you. In the Premier League right now, I feel there are a couple of non-negotiables: you’ve got to run more than the other team if you want to win, or at least get close enough that it doesn’t make that much of a difference. Tottenham ran five kilometres more than Manchester United.”

Physical metrics such as distance run and number of sprints are increasingly accessible and easy to understand, so have fallen into common use. It’s become a common theme that, when a big club fail to meet expectations, pundits and commentators look to their running metrics in search of one catch-all explanation. Liverpool and Chelsea were the targets of similar judgment last season.

articles.title: Chess: World No 11, Anish Giri, leads She Plays to Win women to unlikely victory
articles.summary: Newly promoted SPTW were expected to be outclassed in the top division of the 4NCL British League, but proved a revelation. She Plays to Win Lionesses, the all-female team which won successive promotions to the first division of Britain’s Four Nations Chess League (4NCL) were expected to be…
body: SPTW wanted to continue without male players in the season’s 2026-27 renewal, but the league stood by its rule, introduced to promote women’s chess, that top division teams must include at least one player of each sex.

SPTW’s manager, IM Lorin D’Costa, who doubles as the England women’s coach, then took the bold step of hiring GM Anish Giri, the Netherlands No 1 and world No 11, for last weekend’s two seasonal opening fixtures. SPTW is a charity whose stated objectives are to help girls and young women play chess.
Giri is the highest rated player to compete in the 4NCL for several seasons. The Netherlands’ top female player, IM Eline Roebers, came as well.

Giri won his opening game in crushing style last Saturday in just 24 moves with a direct attack on GM Alexander Cherniaev’s king. The elite GM had done his homework, for the ex-Russian GM Cherniaev, 57, who learnt his skills in the former Soviet Union, has been vulnerable to tactical slugfests throughout his career.

articles.title: Munster to remember 'special' Foley 10 years after his death
articles.summary: Denis Leamy, Tadhg Beirne and Peter O'Mahony speak about Anthony Foley as Munster prepare to honour their former captain and head coach on the 10th anniversary of his death.
body: European nights are invariably significant occasions for Munster, but this Saturday will be especially poignant as they remember one of the greats.

Friday marks 10 years since the death of Anthony Foley. With Munster in Paris before facing Racing 92, Foley - head coach at the time - died suddenly in his sleep aged 42 after a heart condition caused fluid to build up in his lungs.
Having captained Munster to the 2006 Heineken Cup during a stellar playing career that also yielded 62 Ireland caps, the outpouring of grief that followed his passing was remarkable.

Foley - affectionately known as 'Axel' - has never been far from Munster minds in the decade since, but his immense contributions to the province will be highlighted by a series of tributes during their Investec Champions Cup game on Saturday which, coincidentally, pits them against Racing.

articles.title: Arsenal confirm knee procedure for Cerci after persistent issue
articles.summary: Selina Cerci has undergone a knee procedure after an issue that had troubled her since pre-season worsened despite her remaining involved in training. Photo by Sarah Ray-Gain/Getty Images.
body: Selina Cerci has undergone a procedure on the knee problem that has troubled her since pre-season, with Arsenal manager Renee Slegers confirming the decision was taken after her symptoms became too much to continue managing.
Cerci had remained involved in most training sessions despite the problem and was able to play, but her integration into the team was affected.
Recently, she withdrew from the Germany squad with knee problems on October 8, having played only 40 minutes for Arsenal this season.
Slegers said the issue had been present during pre-season and eventually reached the point where further investigation was required.

articles.title: Crane 'buzzing' at England recall, wants more than Insta celebrity
articles.summary: Mason Crane said he was "buzzing" to be back in the England fold, adding that his ambitions go beyond being a "highlights reel" leg-spinner as he looks to make the most of his second bite at international cricket.
body: Crane was capped three times as a 20-year-old, nine years ago, the last of which was his Test debut in the final match of England's 2017/18 Ashes tour in Sydney. He'd take a single wicket as the tourists signed off a 4-0 series drubbing with another defeat.

Speaking to the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, Crane admitted that he was "resigned to the fact it may not come again" as a near decade passed without further recognition, until getting the call for England's upcoming ODI tri-series in Pakistan.
"I didn't really expect it, to be honest," Crane said. "It was a bit out of the blue. But it's really cool and I'm buzzing.
"I think there was a period a few years ago where I was sort of resigned to the fact it may not come again, where I maybe put a bit too much pressure on myself and wasn't particularly enjoying it.

articles.title: Rutter scores twice as Brighton win big and go top in Conference League
articles.summary: Georginio Rutter scored twice and set up one as Brighton thrashed Kauno Zalgris 4-0 to get their Conference League campaign off to a winning start.
body: Brighton were dominant from the first whistle to the last against the Lithuanian Cup winners and took the lead through Rutter, but only after a VAR check. The ball had initially been deemed to have gone out of play before Ibrahim Osman's cut-back to the Frenchman, but the goal was awarded after review.

Rutter then turned provider as Brighton doubled their lead on the stroke of half-time when Hinshelwood - returning to the side for the first time since the Premier League opening weekend - slotted into the corner.
The third came after a lung-bursting run from Malick Yalcouye, who played Osman through to cross for Rutter to turn into the net with ease.

Matt O'Riley made it four with a header as he scored his first Brighton goal since August 2025. The Australia international should have got his second with another header late on, but was denied by an excellent save from Tomas Svedkauskas.
